earlier_scan.source_named: Onziga, Yuga Juma and Leoma Gilley 2012. Phonology of Kakuwa (Kakwa). Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages 10 (sil.org blocked by Cloudflare, not in Wayback)

sources.citation: Onziga, Yuga Juma and Leoma Gilley. 2012. Phonology of Kakuwâ (Kakwa). In Russell J. Norton (ed.), Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages No. 10, 1-15. Nairobi: SIL International.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing: the words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur in the paper. Section III 'Tone' (journal pp. 11-13, PDF pp. 16-18) describes Kakuwâ as a tone language with two level tones (High, Low) plus a Falling tone, lexical and grammatical tone, and downstep; Section IV notes first syllables generally carry a single level tone while final syllables may carry complex tones.
No phonology content; cites Onziga & Gilley 2012 only.

sources.citation: Vossen, Rainer. 1982. The Eastern Nilotes: Linguistic and Historical Reconstructions (Kölner Beiträge zur Afrikanistik 9). Berlin: Dietrich Reimer. [Rosetta Project excerpt, pp. 159-160, section 7.1.2 Kakwa]
sources.note: Excerpt covers only speaker numbers and informants for Kakwa; no phonology in the excerpt. Full book not accessible.
